seen_animation: A four-legged stick-line dog (long neck, boxy rear body, angular hanging legs) stands left of a tree facing left with its head raised high in frames 1-4. In frame 5 the head comes down level, and in frame 6 it drops low toward the ground on the left. In frames 7-8 the dog turns in place: the body compresses into a narrow, foreshortened shape, and by frame 8 the head appears on the right side of the body. From frame 9 on the dog faces right with its head lowered, and it advances right and slightly down across frames 9-16, growing a little larger. By frames 15-16 it stands just above and left of the grey bucket with its snout down toward it. The grey scenery (cloud, tree, bucket, grass, diagonal line) shifts to follow the dog, as if the camera pans right and down.
seen_film: A dog stands on a path beside a person in a dark coat, facing left toward the person with its head raised (frames 1-4). In frame 5 it lowers its head toward the ground on the left. In frames 6-8 it turns around in a quick, blurred motion. In frames 9-13 it walks toward the camera and to the right, facing the viewer, toward a metal basin in the lower right. In frames 14-16 the camera pans right and down, and the dog reaches the basin and lowers its head over it.
named_subject: a dog (the doodle's long-necked four-legged animal)
evidence: Frames 1-4: head raised facing left, matching the film's dog looking up at the person. Frames 5-6: head lowers to the left, matching film frame 5. Frames 7-8: a foreshortened turn in place, matching the film's blurred turn in frames 6-8. Frames 9-13: the dog faces right, head down, and moves toward the bucket while the scenery shifts, matching the film's approach. Frames 14-16: the scenery pans right and down and the dog arrives at the bucket with its snout lowered, matching film frames 14-16. The construction (eye inside an angular head outline, small open snout, boxy rear, split hanging legs) stays recognizable in every frame except the compressed turn.
primary_gap: During the turn in frames 7-8 the drawing collapses into a cramped, overlapping cluster of legs and head, so the doodle's construction is harder to read there than anywhere else, and in frames 15-16 the snout sits to the right of the bucket rather than over it as in the film.
closes_when: Frames 7-8 show the body as one legible foreshortened shape with legs that do not stack on top of each other, and frames 15-16 place the snout directly over the bucket's rim.
protect: The head-up, head-down, turn, approach, arrive-at-bucket timing that matches the film frame for frame; the camera-follow pan of the grey scenery; the doodle's stroke habits (angular head with eye, open snout, boxy rear, split hanging legs); the gradual growth in size as the dog approaches.
identity_gap: The character matches the doodle in all frames except 7-8, where the turn crowds the strokes together so the doodle's shape is only partly readable.
